identity: University of Amsterdam, Italian Studies, registered as Italiaanse Taal en Cultuur (Italian Language and Culture), RIO 56809, registry row 423. The reviewed standard full-time pathway lasts three years. The part-time listing is the same curriculum over six years. Dutch programme metadata and course-specific Italian instruction were both reviewed.
components: The first year also includes a required Dutch writing diagnostic. Tutoring and study guidance continue each year. These requirements carry no credits.

Choose 30 EC of electives, a minor, an internship or eligible study abroad. Courses at another institution require approval. The usual first-year course limit is 12 EC, with specified exceptions up to 24 EC.

progression.yearOne: Course 2 requires prior attendance in course 1. Course 3 requires completion of courses 1 and 2. Course 4 also expects course 3 attendance. History of Italian requires passes in 1 and 2 and attendance in 3 and 4. The diagnostic writing test and annual tutoring are mandatory noncredit requirements, described in the audience notes.
progression.yearTwo: Course 5 requires passes in courses 1–4, and 6 additionally requires attendance in 5. The philosophy and Italian cinema units explicitly require positive binding study advice. The guide places the 30 EC compulsory stay in the second semester, after the six taught language units. The official entry describes Italian-taught bachelor-level courses within the degree’s research directions at approved Erasmus partners. Host-specific courses are not assumed.
progression.yearThree: Translation requires the Italian proficiency units. Good Italy, Bad Italy requires previous programme courses to have been taken. The thesis requires all compulsory components passed and assesses independent research and written academic Italian. The separate 30 EC choice allows eligible electives, a minor, an internship or approved study abroad. The usual introductory-level cap is 12 EC, with specified exceptions up to 24 EC. External coursework requires approval and a minor cannot duplicate compulsory courses.
